title: Bookmarked page
idea: A paper page with Shelf's bookmark cut out at its head, set in an even margin with the page running on below its tail, the way a ribbon lies in a book. It is the swap at its simplest, two levels with the paper standing for the page you saved; it leaves listening out on purpose to test whether the bookmark alone carries Shelf, and on paper the same drawing becomes a dark book with a light bookmark.
built: Page 40 x 55 dp (1 : 1.375, close to A4), centred on the canvas, its corners r 3.3 dp, the bookmark's own shoulder radius, so page and bookmark share one corner language; the corners reach 32.7 of the 33 dp safe radius. Bookmark 28 dp wide with today's proportions (geom.bookmark's defaults scaled), 6 dp below the page's top edge and 6 dp in from each side, so it sits in an even margin on three sides; about 14 dp of page carries on below its tips, enough for the paper to read as a page. The narrowest paper is the 6 dp margin, above the 4.5 dp that becomes 3 px at 48.
small: Every cut keeps both levels and every edge except the notch lies on whole pixels: 5.0%, 5.0% and 5.8% soft at 48, 32 and 16 px, against the solid reference's 3.5, 6.3 and 14.7. 48 px: page 26 x 36 with r 2, bookmark 18 x 22 with a 6 px notch, margins 4 px, 10 px of page below. 32 px: page 18 x 24 with r 1.5, bookmark 12 x 15 with a 4 px notch, margins 3 px, 6 below. 16 px: page 10 x 14 with square corners, bookmark 6 x 8 with a 3 px notch at 45 degrees, margins 2 px, 4 below. Glyph: page 14 x 20 with r 1, bookmark 10 x 12 with a 3 px notch, margins 2 px.
risks: It is the most literal option: a page with a bookmark is a familiar 'bookmarked document' pictogram, so it relies on Shelf's square shoulders and shallow notch to be its own. It says nothing about listening. A light portrait card on a dark tile could be taken for a phone or a cards app at a glance. The page is narrower than a disc, so it looks slighter than its neighbours on a home screen (26% paper against the solid reference's 33%), and at 16 px it nearly fills the tile's height, with 1 px of tile above and below.
